newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia defends shooting of Turkish fisherman.
newsitem.headline: Russia defends shooting of Turkish fisherman.

text.p: Russian border officials on Thursday defended the fatal shooting of a Turkish fisherman caught in Georgia's Black Sea territorial waters.

"We are of course sorry for this tragic incident but the border guards acted in accordance with the law," Mikhail Shekhalevich, head of the Russian border guards international relations department, told a news briefing.

The shooting occurred on March 12 when Russian coastguard cutters, which patrol the area under an agreement with the Georgian government, were sent to intercept nine Turkish vessels spotted in the former Soviet republic's territorial waters.
One fishing boat responded in a dangerous way, officials said, prompting the Russian shooting.
Georgian President Eduard Shevardnadze expressed regret over the incident and the country's foreign ministry lodged an official complaint.
"Even fishing a tonne of fish from our territorial waters is not worth the loss of a human life," Shevardnadze said.
Shekhalevich said some Georgian officials were using the incident to cast Russia in a bad light. He also said that Georgia had not paid its share for maintaining Russian border guards in the region.
